proposals.announcement_evidence: for reactive armor kits, cold start kits and supplemental air transport kits for Armored Multi-Purpose Vehicles
proposals.lexicon_quote: The Armored Multi-Purpose Vehicle (AMPV)	2944G80819	350	Armored Multi Purpose Vehicle (AMPV)
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the program in the index's own words (differing only by the leading article and the acronym gloss), the awardee is BAE Systems Land & Armaments at York, Pennsylvania -- the AMPV prime -- and the action is a modification (P00006) to BAE's AMPV production contract W56HZV-23-C-0024. The money colour matches the line exactly: 'Fiscal 2023 and 2024 weapons and tracked combat vehicle procurement, Army funds in the amount of $19,500,242 were obligated', and 2944G80819 is the WTCV procurement BLI whose title is 'Armored Multi Purpose Vehicle (AMPV)' (doc 350). Reactive armor kits, cold start kits and air-transport kits delivered on the AMPV production contract are configuration content of the vehicle this line buys, not a service wrapped around someone else's platform. The only other owner of the name in this index is 0203735A, an RDT&E rollup ('Combat Vehicle Improvement Programs') that procurement appropriations do not fund; I record it separately as weak so the collision is visible.

refute_a.reason: Money: the paragraph obligates 'Fiscal 2023 and 2024 weapons and tracked combat vehicle procurement, Army funds' and budget_lines puts 2944G80819 at account 2033A, exhibit P-1 (doc 350 = Procurement of Weapons and Tracked Combat Vehicles) -> 021-2033, the same appropriation the text names; the lake carries no funding account on W56HZV23C0024 (0 of 43 rows non-null), so money_color_ok treats the award colour as unknown rather than disjoint and the stated colour stands unrebutted, while the only competing owner of the AMPV name, 0203735A, is 2040A RDT&E and cannot spend WTCV procurement. Mission: reactive armor, cold start and supplemental air transport kits delivered by the AMPV prime (BAE Land & Armaments, York) as mod P00006 to the AMPV production contract are configuration content of the very vehicle this line buys -- no index row anywhere owns 'reactive armor', 'cold start' or 'air transport' kits, and the one plausible alternative WTCV owner, 6652GM1900 VEHICLE PROTECTION SYSTEMS, owns only active-protection names (MAC/MAF/LWR/TAP/VBK) -- so the AMPV is the program the PE funds, not a platform the award merely supports. Rollup: title 'Armored Multi Purpose Vehicle (AMPV)' is a single-program P-1 line, matches no CATCHALL_TITLE pattern and is not an org-split key. Precedent agrees: chunk_000_A record 60 accepted this same PE on this same contract on the same colour.

refute_b.reason: The collision is real but does not transfer the award: 0203735A (A.tsv:41, doc 359) owns the identical name and 'AMPV Improvement Program' (A.tsv:36), yet it is an RDT&E program element while this record obligates FY2023/2024 weapons and tracked combat vehicle PROCUREMENT, and 2944G80819 (A.tsv:994, doc 350) is the only procurement owner of the AMPV name; no index row owns 'reactive armor', 'cold start' or 'air transport kit', the name is the index's own wording rather than an invented alias, the M-variant is not contested by any competing row, and the evidence is the program name plus a production-contract mod, not merely BAE's contractor name.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for Phased Array Tracking Radar to Intercept on Target missile support center, missile assessments, testing, recertification, and repair activities

First, the evidence is the bare spelled-out PATRIOT platform name with no program qualifier: this index exposes Patriot through three PEs (Patriot Mods 0962C50700, Patriot Product Improvement 0607865A, and the MSE/PAC-3 side), and every name those lines own -- PIP, MSE, ADI, IESP, TPW, TPX-57, PCSB -- is absent from the text, so nothing in the announcement chooses an owner. proposals.announcement_evidence: for engineering services, configuration management and technical support for the Mounted Assured Position, Navigation and Timing System Gen II
proposals.lexicon_quote: Mounted APNT System (MAPS)	9897K49000	346	Assured Positioning, Navigation and Timing
proposals.rationale: The announcement writes out in full the acronym the index abbreviates: 'Mounted Assured Position, Navigation and Timing System' is 'Mounted APNT System (MAPS)' and nothing else, and MAPS GEN II is the fielded increment of that same system rather than a different program. The awardee is Collins Aerospace, Cedar Rapids, the MAPS producer, on MAPS contract W56KGY-22-F-0074, and the obligation is 'Fiscal 2023 other procurement, Army funds', which is exactly the appropriation of 9897K49000 (doc 346, 'Assured Positioning, Navigation and Timing'). The two-way collision with 0604120A (doc 353, the RDT&E PNT line) resolves on the same fact: OPA money is production money, not advanced development, and I record the RDT&E member separately as weak. One caveat lens A should test honestly: the scope is engineering services, configuration management and technical support rather than units of hardware, so the claim rests on those being the production-support content the procurement line funds for the system it buys -- the same reading two earlier chunks accepted for MAPS GEN II production support.

refute_a.reason: Money holds on both sides independently: the text obligates 'Fiscal 2023 other procurement, Army funds' and all 20 lake rows on W56KGY22F0074 (Rockwell Collins/Collins Aerospace, $88.9M obligated) carry exactly one federal account, 021-2035, which is 9897K49000's own account 2035A -- procurement money on a doc-346 Other Procurement, Army line, with no O&M dollar anywhere in the action, so the held-out study's O&M-attached-to-a-procurement-line inversion is absent; this is the mirror image of the chunk_118_A refutation, where the same program name sat on an order funded from 017-1109 Procurement, Marine Corps, and the RDT&E competitor 0604120A is 2040A and excluded by colour. Mission: MAPS is the system this OPA line buys (its narrative enumerates ALTNAV/DAPS/MAPS), and engineering services, configuration management and technical support for MAPS GEN II charged to that line's own procurement appropriation is production-support content of the line, not work wrapped around some other program's platform. Rollup: 'Assured Positioning, Navigation and Timing' is a named P-1 line with named sub-efforts, not a threshold/'other'/'miscellaneous' aggregate. One caveat recorded rather than suppressed: unlike the accepted chunk_065_A precedent, whose text said 'in support of production', this paragraph names no hardware and no production, so the services-versus-generic-support reading rests on the appropriation the Army actually charged rather than on the words -- procurement colour verified on both sides is enough not to refute, but this is the thinnest of the three proposals.

refute_b.reason: The alias is genuine -- the announcement spells out in full the acronym A.tsv:1428 abbreviates -- and although 0604120A (A.tsv:566, doc 353) owns the identical 'Mounted APNT System (MAPS)' string, doc 346 is the Other Procurement Army volume and the record obligates FY2023 other procurement, which an RDT&E program element cannot take; within OPA 9897K49000 is the sole owner of the MAPS name (8662A01006 is aviation EGI/MAGNA, 0604805A is CMFF, 0205778A is GMLRS APNT), and no row in the index qualifies a GEN increment, so 'Gen II' names the fielded increment of the same system rather than a distinct program -- the residual doubt is the services scope, which is lens A's question, not identity.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for 50 recapitalized M1120A4 Heavy Expanded Mobility Tactical Trucks
proposals.lexicon_quote: Heavy Expanded Mobility Tactical Truck (HEMTT)	8309DA0500	346	Family Of Heavy Tactical Vehicles (FHTV)
proposals.rationale: The end item is named in the index's own words with a unit count and an A4 variant designator -- '50 recapitalized M1120A4 Heavy Expanded Mobility Tactical Trucks' -- delivered by Oshkosh Defense on FHTV recapitalisation contract W56HZV-15-D-0031, and 8309DA0500 ('Family Of Heavy Tactical Vehicles (FHTV)') is the line whose narrative owns both the HEMTT name and its A4 load-handling variant, the M1120A4 being the HEMTT LHS. The appropriation matches the line's colour: 'Fiscal 2016 other procurement (Army) funds in the amount of $19,286,100 were obligated', and doc 346 is the other-procurement volume. The trucks themselves are the line's own end item, so this is not the platform trap. The one competing owner of the HEMTT name, 0604114A, carries 'M983A4 Heavy Expanded Mobility Tactical Truck (HEMTT)' only as the carrier vehicle for the Lower Tier Air Missile Defense sensor -- a platform that line rides on -- and this award buys recapitalised trucks, not a radar they haul, so the collision resolves against it.

refute_a.reason: Money: the text obligates 'Fiscal 2016 other procurement (Army) funds in the amount of $19,286,100' and all 92 lake rows on W56HZV15D0031 (Oshkosh Defense) carry 021-2035;097-0350, intersecting 8309DA0500's account 2035A -> 021-2035, so procurement money lands on the doc-346 Other Procurement, Army line with no O&M inversion, while the only other owner of the HEMTT name, 0604114A, is 2040A RDT&E. Mission: 50 recapitalized M1120A4 Heavy Expanded Mobility Tactical Trucks are the FHTV line's own end item rebuilt under its procurement-funded RECAP program -- the M1120A4 is the HEMTT Load Handling System variant, a name the same PE's narrative separately owns ('The HEMTT A4 Load Handling System (LHS)') -- so the trucks are what the line buys, not a platform the award supports for somebody else's sensor. Rollup: 'Family Of Heavy Tactical Vehicles (FHTV)' is a defined vehicle-family P-1 line with its own enumerated members, matching no CATCHALL_TITLE pattern ('less than/under/< $', '^other', '^miscellaneous'). Precedent agrees twice over: chunk_118_A record 67 and chunk_072_A record 15 both accepted this PE on this very contract, including on pre-FY2017 money, and the fact that ingested budget_lines rows for this PE begin at FY2017 while the funds are FY2016 is a J-book edition coverage artefact, not an appropriation or mission defect lens A can refute on.

refute_b.reason: Both lens-B prongs resolve against the alternatives: the other owner of the HEMTT name, 0604114A (A.tsv:541, doc 353), carries only the M983A4 tractor as the LTAMDS carrier and is RDT&E, whereas this award buys M1120A4 trucks -- the A4 load-handling variant 8309DA0500 itself owns at A.tsv:1292 -- with FY2016 other procurement Army funds; the nearest same-appropriation candidate, 8992DA0924 'Modification Of In Svc Equip' (doc 346), owns only the FHTV family name and not HEMTT or the A4 LHS, and this action buys 50 whole recapitalised trucks by quantity rather than modification kits, while 0604622A (doc 355) owns only the generic 'Heavy Tactical Vehicles (HTV)' and is likewise RDT&E.
